patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with Addison disease who joins in 2022; Hashimoto hypothyroidism completes autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2, then celiac disease, vitiligo, rheumatoid arthritis and alopecia areata follow. In 2025 she converts to Graves disease, has thyroid storm and a thyroidectomy, and in July 2026 an adrenal crisis on the morning of a planned cholecystectomy.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to transfer her primary care here; her old office is dropping her plan's network for membership and she'd rather have a doctor she can text. Records release sent for her prior primary-care office and she says her adrenal doctor is with an outside endocrinology group, she'll bring her med bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F teacher transferring care.

Adrenal: primary adrenal insufficiency diagnosed in her mid-20s (per pt; records requested). Managed by an outside endocrinology group, seen about yearly. On hydrocortisone 20 mg on waking and 10 mg around 4 pm, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Knows to double hydrocortisone with fever; has never needed the ED for it.

Other hx: iron deficiency anemia some years ago, took ferrous sulfate for several months at the old office, finished, no repeat that she knows of. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.

Meds as above. NKDA.

Family: mother has type 1 diabetes and Hashimoto. Sister with vitiligo. Maternal aunt also has adrenal insufficiency.

Social: married, teaches second grade. Never smoked, doesn't drink. Walks most evenings.

ROS: energy so-so by late afternoon, which she puts down to the job. Otherwise negative.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted, BMI ~24. Skin normal color, no hyperpigmentation of creases or gums. Thyroid not enlarged to my exam. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft. No edema.

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency - stable on current replacement. CMP today for Na/K. Continue meds; refills here are fine, endo sets doses. Asked her to keep her endo visits.
2. Hx iron deficiency anemia - CBC today.
3. Health maintenance - Pap with HPV collected today. HIV and hep C screen once. Tdap given (last one she can't recall). Flu/COVID at a fall nurse visit.
Return for physical next summer or sooner as needed.

documents.title: Results from your visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Riley - your sodium and potassium look right where they should on your fludrocortisone, kidney and liver numbers are normal, and your blood count is normal with no sign of the old anemia. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. The Pap and HPV test were both normal, so that's done for five years. Talk soon.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: medical records
documents.body:
42 pages received by fax from the patient's previous primary-care office, covering about six years. Summary for the chart:
- Primary adrenal insufficiency on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone, managed by outside endocrinology; copies of two endocrine letters, both stable.
- Iron deficiency anemia on an older CBC, treated with oral iron; follow-up CBC normal.
- Annual exams with normal BMPs and CBCs. Prior cervical cytology normal.
- Allergies: none known.
Filed to media. Nothing outstanding.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after school for flu (L deltoid) and bivalent COVID booster (R deltoid). Reviewed: she knows to take her stress dose of hydrocortisone if she runs a fever afterward. Waited 15 min, no reaction.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Tired for most of the past year even with 8 hours of sleep; she had chalked it up to work but it's worse this fall. Hair feels coarse and is breaking. Husband says her eyes look puffy in the mornings. Constipated more days than not. No fever, no neck pain, has not lost weight. Taking hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone every day, no missed doses, no salt craving or dizziness.

O: Vitals as charted. Skin dry, a little cool. Thyroid feels diffusely enlarged and firm, no discrete nodule, not tender. Heart regular. Reflexes slow to relax at the ankles.

A/P: Fatigue with dry skin, hair change and a goiter. With her Addison disease and her mother's Hashimoto, autoimmune hypothyroidism is first on the list. TSH, free T4 today; BMP and CBC to make sure the adrenal side and the old anemia aren't part of it. Will message results. If the thyroid is off I'll ask her endocrinologist to see her sooner rather than at her spring visit.

orders.reason: TSH 16.8, free T4 0.5, goiter; known Addison disease

documents.title: Thyroid results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Riley, your thyroid is underactive: TSH 16.8 (high) and free T4 0.5 (low). That fits how you've been feeling. Electrolytes and blood count were fine. I've sent a referral and called your endocrinology office; they can see you on the 21st instead of March. Because thyroid and adrenal treatment interact, I'd like them to start the thyroid medicine. Hang in there.

documents.title: RE: Thyroid results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you!! honestly relieved there's a reason. I'll be there on the 21st.

conditions.label: Autoimmune polyglandular failure
conditions.note: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2: Addison disease with Hashimoto thyroiditis.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily on an empty stomach

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Date of visit: 12/21/2022
Re: Riley Fenton, DOB 11/21/1989

Thank you for moving Ms. Fenton up. She has been fatigued for roughly a year in spite of adequate sleep, and describes coarser, brittle hair, some puffiness around the eyes and constipation. She has had no fever, weight loss or anterior neck pain. Her adrenal replacement is unchanged: hydrocortisone 20 mg in the morning and 10 mg in the afternoon, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. She takes nothing else. No drug allergies.

Family history is notable for type 1 diabetes and Hashimoto disease in her mother, vitiligo in a sister and primary adrenal insufficiency in a maternal aunt. Never smoker, no alcohol. Teaches elementary school.

Exam: pulse 54, BP 110/70, BMI 24. Skin dry and cool. The thyroid is diffusely enlarged and firm, nontender, with no nodules felt. Deep tendon reflexes show a delayed relaxation phase, clearest at the ankle.

Labs today: TSH 18 uIU/mL, free T4 0.4 ng/dL, total T3 60 ng/dL. Anti-thyroglobulin antibody positive. Serum cholesterol elevated, as expected with this degree of hypothyroidism; we will not treat it until she is euthyroid.

Impression: Hashimoto thyroiditis with overt hypothyroidism. Together with her Addison disease this is autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2. Her adrenal replacement was already in place, which is the order we want before thyroid hormone.

Plan: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, on an empty stomach, apart from food and other pills. Continue current hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. TSH in 6 to 8 weeks. Given the syndrome, we would screen periodically for other autoimmune conditions; she is aware her family history is relevant.

Allergies: NKDA.
cc: primary care

documents.title: Outside letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Endo letter reviewed. Hashimoto hypothyroidism, APS-2 with her Addison's. Levothyroxine 112 started by endo, added to our list. Endo following TSH.

documents.title: Electronic refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
eRx renewal requests for hydrocortisone 10 mg tabs (#90, 2 qAM + 1 qPM) and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg (#90). Last BMP 12/6 normal. Sent to PCP queue.

PCP: approved x 90 days with 3 refills each.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Check-in 3 months after starting levothyroxine. Energy a little better. Honest that she forgets the levothyroxine a couple of mornings a week - the hydrocortisone is habit, the new pill isn't, and she takes it with coffee on the way out the door. Endo drew a TSH in February; she doesn't know the number and it isn't in our system.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thyroid still full. Heart regular.

A/P: Hypothyroidism, partly treated, adherence the main issue. Talked through taking it at bedtime or keeping it next to the hydrocortisone, 30-60 min before coffee. Phone alarm set during the visit. BMP for the adrenal side today. Will ask endo for their February labs. Physical in August.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 3:40 follow-up. Texted; she replied that a parent conference ran over and she forgot to call. Not rebooked at her request, will see us at the August physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 33F.

Interval: saw a gynecologist in late June for cycles spacing out to every 2-3 months and a year of trying for a pregnancy. She says they found her thyroid way off again (TSH 12) and a mildly high prolactin they thought came from the thyroid, and asked that we recheck both in about two months. We don't have their letter yet - requested again today. Since then: levothyroxine every night at bedtime, pill organizer next to the hydrocortisone, hasn't missed since. Feels more like herself. Weight up a bit over the spring, holding now.

Adrenal: no sick days this year. Endo visit due fall.

Meds: levothyroxine 112 mcg qHS, hydrocortisone 20/10, fludrocortisone 0.1. NKDA.
Social unchanged. Never smoker, no alcohol.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted. Skin less dry than in the spring. Thyroid mildly enlarged, smooth. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Reflexes normal today. No edema.

A/P
1. Hashimoto hypothyroidism / APS-2 - TSH and prolactin today at gyn's request. CMP for Na/K.
2. Lipids today; endo noted cholesterol was up when she was hypothyroid.
3. Irregular cycles / trying to conceive - per gyn, the plan hinges on the thyroid; they'll take it from here once they see the numbers.
4. HM: Pap 2022 normal. Flu/COVID in October.
Return 6 months.

documents.title: Your physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: TSH is 3.1 now, in range, and prolactin came back at 14, which is normal - so the gynecologist's hunch that the thyroid was behind it looks right. Cholesterol is normal now that the thyroid is treated. Sodium/potassium, kidney, liver and blood count all normal. I'm faxing these to your gynecologist. Keep doing exactly what you're doing with the bedtime dose.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology practice
Date of service: 06/26/2023
Patient: Riley Fenton, 33 y.o.

Reason for visit: menstrual irregularity and difficulty conceiving.

HPI: Ms. Fenton has APS type 2 with Hashimoto thyroiditis, diagnosed this past winter, and Addison disease. For about six months her periods have come only every two to three months. She and her husband have been trying to conceive for a year without success. She also notes tiredness, some weight gain and feeling cold. She acknowledges she has not been taking her levothyroxine reliably.

Medications: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily (missed often), hydrocortisone 20 mg AM / 10 mg PM, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with T1DM and Hashimoto; sister vitiligo; maternal aunt adrenal insufficiency.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: vitals within normal limits. Weight 67 kg. Skin dry. Reflexes with a slowed relaxation phase.

Labs: TSH 12 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 0.7 ng/dL (0.9-1.7), prolactin 29 ng/mL (4-23).

Assessment: oligomenorrhea and subfertility in the setting of undertreated primary hypothyroidism. The mild prolactin elevation is most likely secondary to the hypothyroidism.

Plan: daily levothyroxine adherence reviewed at length. Repeat TSH and prolactin in about 8 weeks through her primary care physician. We will reassess cycles and fertility once she is euthyroid; she will call us.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Outside letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gyn letter from June finally here. Matches what pt told us. Our 8/22 recheck (TSH 3.1, PRL 14) already faxed to them. Filed.

documents.body: Flu vaccine L arm, 2023-24 COVID R arm. Tolerated both. Stress-dose reminder given for any fever. Observed 15 min.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: belly pain and bloating, on and off since late spring.

Crampy lower belly pain and bloating, worse after eating, especially big meals. Some days loose stools. No blood, no black stools, no fever, weight steady. No travel, no new meds. Thyroid pills every night, adrenal meds as usual. She wondered about celiac herself because of all the autoimmune things.

Exam: well, vitals as charted. Abdomen soft, not distended, mildly tender low on both sides, no rebound, no guarding, no masses. 

A/P: Postprandial pain and bloating with loose stools in a woman with APS-2 - celiac disease is high on the list. tTG-IgA and total IgA today; she has NOT gone gluten-free yet, and I asked her not to until this is sorted. Will refer to GI if positive.

orders.reason: tTG IgA 86 U/mL with normal total IgA; bloating, postprandial pain

documents.title: Celiac blood test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Riley - the celiac antibody (tTG-IgA) is positive at 86; anything over 15 is positive, and your total IgA is normal so the test is reliable. This strongly points to celiac disease. The standard next step is an endoscopy with small bowel biopsies by GI, and it only works if you're still eating gluten, so please keep eating normally until then. Referral is in; they should call within the week.

documents.title: RE: Celiac blood test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ugh, not surprised. Will keep eating bread for now lol. GI called already, Dec 18.
